questions.question: If your vehicle has a header board, it should:

options.text: Be damaged.
Be loose.
Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, check that the header board is secure, has no damage, and is strong enough to hold cargo.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Lock up your wheels.
Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers.
See the outside of the bus.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the inside rearview mirror watches passenger activity. It should be adjusted so you can see all students, including those directly behind you.

questions.question: When approaching a curve on the driving test, you must do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes steadily throughout the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down before entering so you don't need to brake or shift during the curve. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the right, then back into it. Move the rear of your vehicle as close as possible to the back of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space's boundaries.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror of a school bus is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.
See in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the inside rearview mirror watches passenger activity.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against you.
You should pull-up at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
Some examiners accept excessive pull-ups.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up is when you stop and pull forward to get a better position. Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
Within five feet of where the examiner said.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of where the examiner said.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner describes. Failing to complete an exercise exactly as described can result in failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check that:

options.text: The pedal surface has been smoothed out.
The gas pedal sticks.
Nothing blocks the pedals.
Something is underneath the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing blocks the pedals.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that could stop them from working. Make sure the pedals work properly and that the surfaces are grooved if needed.

questions.question: Where should students stay during an emergency?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control on the bus. However, if staying on the bus is dangerous, the driver should move them to a safe location.

questions.question: On the road test, you will be graded on lane usage. Which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Driving in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: During the road test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, finish turns in the correct lane. Always stay in or move to the rightmost lane, unless it is blocked.

questions.question: Which is most likely to cause student deaths per year?

options.text: Students getting on or off a school bus
Accidents with drunk drivers
Accidents caused by careless driving
Accidents when drivers ignore traffic signals or signs

questions.correctAnswerText: Students getting on or off a school bus
questions.explanation: More students are killed each year while getting on or off school buses than while riding inside them.

questions.question: When should you check the mirrors on a bus?

options.text: Before you drive the bus
While you are driving the bus
After you drive the bus
You do not need to check the mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you drive the bus
questions.explanation: Always check the bus mirrors before you start driving. Adjust them as needed before you begin.

questions.question: Except for the straight line backing exercise, you may exit your vehicle to check its position up to:

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times
questions.explanation: You may exit your vehicle to check its position during any test exercise. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look only once. For any other exercise, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, are drivers allowed to exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: No, you are not allowed to exit the vehicle
You are discouraged from exiting the vehicle
You can exit only if the vehicle is in reverse
You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set

questions.correctAnswerText: You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting. You may check the position up to two times, except for straight line backing, where you may check only once.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, when should you use your four-way flashers?

options.text: Before crossing railroad tracks
Never use them
Only after crossing railroad tracks
Only near railroad tracks if a train is coming

questions.correctAnswerText: Before crossing railroad tracks
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off once your entire vehicle has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the test, you must:

options.text: Never touch the handrail
Always hold the handrail
Exit quickly

questions.correctAnswerText: Always hold the handrail
questions.explanation: When exiting during the test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, always hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle touching or crossing an exercise boundary line
A driver making a single pull-up
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and setting the parking brake
The vehicle stalling while shifting gears

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching or crossing an exercise boundary line
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must show all of the following except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating temperature
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used
questions.explanation: During an oil pressure gauge check, make sure it is working. The gauge should show normal or increasing pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If there is an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: If students cause a problem on the bus while others are getting off, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the back of the bus right away and handle it while students get off
Wait until all students are off, then handle the problem
Have another student handle it while you watch students get off

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are off, then handle the problem
questions.explanation: Watching students load and unload requires your full attention. If a student causes a problem, wait until all students have safely exited the bus before you deal with it.
